ai.description: This 38–80 cm viper is sandy-brown with a series of white, dark-edged dorsal blotches. It features a distinct white arrow-shaped head mark and keeled scales that produce a rasping sound when rubbed.
ai.identificationRemarks: The most reliable diagnostic feature of *Echis carinatus* is the distinct, whitish, arrow-shaped or trident-like marking located on the top of its head.
ai.habitat: The saw-scaled viper inhabits arid to semi-arid regions, including rocky outcrops, scrublands, and sandy plains, typically ranging from sea level up to 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: When threatened, the saw-scaled viper coils into a C-shape and rubs its serrated scales together to produce a distinctive, rasping warning sound.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Echis carinatus* is ovoviviparous, typically breeding during the monsoon season. Females produce litters of 3–15 young, though larger clutches of up to 23 have been recorded.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Echis carinatus* is widely distributed across the Indian subcontinent, primarily inhabiting arid to semi-arid lowlands, scrublands, and plains from sea level up to 2,000m.
